@graph.name: Phasing Models & Continuity Operations
@graph.description: Phasing models and continuity operations for warehouse relocation, published as industry education. Nothing in this dataset is a company offering: the company's published scope is warehouse work planned around the site, and no phasing, sequencing, continuity, or inventory-accuracy service is claimed. Phasing models used across the industry, labeled domain: a phased zone move, moving the building in zones; a big-bang move, everything at once, which industry guidance generally warns against; a wave move, sequenced non-critical stock first, then core SKUs, with equipment last; a velocity-first move, fastest-moving inventory prioritized; and after-hours or weekend moves that keep shipping days clear. The continuity workstream, labeled domain: customer communication that is proactive, specific, and early; scheduling the move around the busiest shipping days; a temporary storage or overflow buffer; backup procedures such as alternate carriers, manual pick lists, and fallback windows; daily check-ins during move week; predictability valued over perfection. Inventory continuity practice, labeled domain: a pre-move full audit and dead-stock purge through the warehouse system; tagged and counted waves mapped from the old location to the new; system locations updated wave by wave; post-move validation through spot checks, a first reconciling cycle count, re-slotting fast movers, updated procedures, and a post-move review. Downtime framing, attributed and domain only: an industry guide (ADSI, 2026) puts average unplanned downtime at $260,000 per hour across manufacturing sectors and frames one delayed shift as potentially exceeding the entire moving invoice — an attributed industry claim, never a company figure and never a downtime guarantee. Timeline guidance, labeled domain: heavy equipment and racking scheduling runs three to six months out; the move week runs in waves; the following week stabilizes and the week after optimizes — planning guidance, never a company lead-time promise.
